about: Design section 7.1's dependency gate (Phase 1b B7, B4 recheck 6 item 2). clippy.toml
disallows destructive paths by name; a dependency could expose an equivalent under
checks this file against Cargo.lock and every workspace manifest. It fails when:
a direct (normal or build) dependency of any workspace crate is not under `direct`;
a dev-only one is not under `dev`; any package in Cargo.lock that can wrap system
calls (libc, linux-raw-sys, rustix, nix, syscalls, sc, any *-sys crate, or one that
depends directly on any of them) is not listed at all; an entry names a package
Cargo.lock lacks, or a kind it does not have; `syscalls` disagrees with Cargo.lock;
a direct entry's `destructive` paths and clippy.toml's paths under that crate differ;
clippy.toml names a crate that is neither std nor a direct entry; or a raw-syscall
crate is direct with no destructive paths. So a new dependency that can reach
system calls joins this file, and its destructive methods join clippy.toml, in the
same change. std is the toolchain's, gated by its clippy.toml paths directly.

hyper-util.why: TokioIo adapters for the Unix-socket transport; its libc use is socket options, with no removal, signal or subprocess API

libc.why: the raw system-call surface: every destructive function is in clippy.toml, reachable only from the approved modules

rusqlite.why: SQLite through bundled libsqlite3-sys; no removal API. SQLite's own -wal/-shm/-journal maintenance is the one dependency-internal unlink (design 7.1)

tokio.why: the async runtime: its file removal, rename, truncation, signal and subprocess APIs are in clippy.toml

tokio-util.why: CancellationToken and task trackers; no file, signal or subprocess API

tonic-prost-build.why: kilnd-api's build script only: generates the gRPC stubs on the build host, linked into no binary

h2.why: raw HTTP/2 clients in admission tests

tempfile.why: test scratch directories; TempDir removes its own on drop. Never a normal dependency

getrandom.why: random numbers for tempfile names and hash seeds

linux-raw-sys.why: rustix's raw Linux bindings, for tempfile

rustix.why: tempfile's system calls; tempfile is dev-only, so rustix is never named by workspace code

signal-hook-registry.why: tokio's signal handling (sigaction, not signal sending)

windows-sys.why: Windows bindings of several crates; not built for Linux or macOS
